findings.claim: The authority for the eight-hour suspensions '(39 Stat. 1192, or sec. 2 of the Act of June 19, 1912) is not contingent on the 1917 war, so the 1921 resolution does not reach it'.
findings.evidence: Sec. 2 of the Act of June 19, 1912, ch. 174, 37 Stat. 137 (govinfo statute/37/137) lets the President waive the Act 'as to any specific contract or contracts during time of war or a time when war is imminent': a war-contingent power. EO 2663 rests only on that section ('by virtue of authority contained in section two of ... (37 Stat., 137)'), and EO 2678 rests on it together with 39 Stat. 1192. 39 Stat. 1192 ('in case of national emergency') is correctly described as not war-tied (it was still used in 1939, e.g. EO 8198). The statement is therefore wrong for EO 2663 and in part for EO 2678.
findings.fix: Split the statement: 39 Stat. 1192 is a standing national-emergency power; sec. 2 of the 1912 Act is a 'during time of war' power, so the 1921 resolution (41 Stat. 1359) does reach that authority, and the cessation of the 1912 waiver power is a disclosed candidate end for EO 2663 (and the 1912 part of EO 2678) under P3/P8. The lead can stay open because these waivers are for specific contracts whose completion is unrecorded, but M14 and the B20 basis must not claim the 1912 authority is war-independent.

findings.location: B15 and B16 (Overman Act branch), M6, M8
findings.claim: Each B15 order's 'only operative content is a redistribution of functions authorized by the Act of May 20, 1918', so the Overman Act's end ends it; the War Industries Board's winding-up 'rest[s] on Overman Act authority'.
findings.evidence: The Overman Act's termination paragraph (40 Stat. 557, verified on govinfo) overrides only 'any authorization of the President under this Act'. Several B15/B16 orders also invoke other authority: EO 3019-A ('by virtue of the authority vested in me as Chief Executive ... as well as by virtue of any and all other Acts of Congress'), EO 3161 and EO 3248-A ('as well as by virtue of any and all other acts of Congress'; EO 3248-A directs payment from named appropriation acts), EO 2929 ('as Chief Executive'). EO 2868, the B16 member, created the War Industries Board under the Council of National Defense provisions of the Act of Aug. 29, 1916, not under the Overman Act. EO 3019-A's own text also caps its exception 1 continuation 'in no event longer than the proclamation of peace', which the doctrine does not use.
findings.fix: State why the Overman termination clause ends orders that also rest on other authority (for example, that the named appropriations lapsed or that the functions reassigned exist only by Overman authority), or move the orders whose other authority is not shown to be spent (at least EO 3248-A, EO 3161, and EO 2868's winding-up) to open with the Overman end as a disclosed candidate. Cite EO 3019-A's 'in no event longer than the proclamation of peace' as its own-terms bound for exception 1.

findings.location: B08 (EO 2884, EO 3100); B07 and B08 lead kinds
findings.claim: EO 2884 and EO 3100 'command only through' offices EO 3320 abolished; lead_kind 'ended_with_abolished_office'; B07 uses 'ended_by_later_instrument' for both EO 2679-A and EO 3087.
findings.evidence: EO 3320 (held, S8) did not abolish the Grain Corporation; it continued it 'as a governmental agency for this purpose only' (liquidation). EO 2884 designates the Grain Corporation as the wheat-buying agency, and EO 3100 authorizes the Corporation's purchases 'under the direction of the United States Wheat Director'. Their reach by EO 3320 depends on reading 'for this purpose only' as an express end of the buying designation, which the basis does not argue. EO 3320 reaches EO 3087 by its date ('Executive Order of May 14, 1919'), but reaches EO 2679-A only by abolishing its subject by name; COORDINATOR_RULINGS P7 prescribes the kind 'ended_by_express_abolition_of_its_subject' for that reach.
findings.fix: Use the P7 lead kind for EO 2679-A, EO 2736 and EO 3143. For EO 2884 and EO 3100, quote 'continuing to act as a governmental agency for this purpose only' as the words that end the purchasing designation and explain the reach, or rest them on the Lever Act's cessation (interval to 1921-03-03; EO 3100 also needs the Act of Mar. 4, 1919's own term).

wrong_member_decisions.why: The outcome (no, revoked by EO 2952) is right, but the lead's date is 1918-06-09. EO 2952 is dated Sept. 6, 1918, and June 9, 1918 precedes EO 2913's own date (July 15, 1918).

Left open because 'no held record shows that [the sale] was made', but held member EO 3265 recites 'the actual sale made by the Alien Property Custodian' under EO 3259 by Apr. 29, 1920. Decidable as exhausted by performance (interval 1920-04-16 to 1920-04-29), or the gap must say so.

The lead stays open, but its basis is wrong for this member: EO 2663 rests solely on sec. 2 of the 1912 eight-hour Act, a 'during time of war or a time when war is imminent' power that the 1921 resolution does reach (candidate end, not 'not contingent on the 1917 war').
Rests on both sec. 2 of the 1912 Act (war-contingent) and 39 Stat. 1192. The basis wrongly treats both as war-independent.

Decided no on the Overman Act's end, but the order also invokes 'any and all other acts of Congress' and directs payment from named appropriation acts. Without a showing that those other authorities are spent, the Overman termination clause ('any authorization of the President under this Act') does not reach the whole command (R6).

The War Industries Board was established under the Council of National Defense provisions of the 1916 Act, not the Overman Act. The claim that the Board's winding-up continuation ended with the Overman Act needs the argument in R6, or the lead should cite EO 3019-A's own cap ('in no event longer than the proclamation of peace') as far as it reaches.

The operative words are a new quit-claim authorization. Amending EO 4073-A is only the stated reason, and the branch's 'amend' regex is satisfied by the TWEA authority recital, not by an operative amending clause (R13).

summary: The engine run reproduces the doctrine's counts: 263 members, 43 decided (18 TERM, 25 ACT), 220 open, 0 contradicted. Most of the structure is sound. The held pins and hashes all match. The statute and treaty texts read on govinfo support the Lever Act, Overman Act and emergency shipping fund mechanisms, and the peace-treaty dates (Nov. 14 and Dec. 20, 1921) and the date bounds derived from them (Sept. 3, 1921; May 14 and June 20, 1922) are right. The undecided list is broadly honest. Three errors must be fixed. First, the 1921 joint resolution is cited throughout at 41 Stat. 1395, but it is at 41 Stat. 1359-1360. Second, B10 dates EO 2913's revocation 1918-06-09, but EO 2952 is dated Sept. 6, 1918, and the wrong date precedes EO 2913 itself. Third, B20 says the eight-hour suspension authority is not war-contingent, but sec. 2 of the 1912 Act (relied on by EO 2663 and 2678) is a 'during time of war' power. Three claims are unsupported. B18's claim that no held record shows performance is false for EO 3259 (EO 3265 recites the actual sale). B02 omits NARA's statement that no EO 3087-A is on record. The Overman Act branches do not address orders that also rest on other authority, or EO 2868's non-Overman origin. The minor findings are that B08's reach to EO 2884 and 3100 through EO 3320 is thinly argued, and a wrong count, the false statement that no member has a held later edge, incomplete or stale gaps, a nonexistent branch reference, lead kinds that are not the coordinator's, and order-date bounds inherited from wrong census dates.
